title: Last 30-minute move, signed
source: price.recent_move
notes: sign from 'rose/fell/moved +-x'; bottom third = flat, middle = small, top = big. Rank is 30-min move vs same minute, last 19-20 sessions.

title: Move since the open vs usual band
source: open.noise_band
notes: 'above/below the usual move-from-the-open band' = outside; 'above the higher / below the lower ... inside or at the edge' = up/down inside; 'between the settled open and yesterday's close' = flat. Label is in sigma not opening-straddle units (rank is unit-free). 09-28 reads use an older template that does not say the side. The older 09-28 template (side not stated) answers None.

title: Afternoon leg since 14:00
source: price.afternoon_leg
notes: only reads at/after 14:45 (at 14:30 the leg since 14:00 is TREND-01's 30 minutes). Sign + tercile like TREND-01. Bug seen: at 14:00 the move is ~0 but ranks 'larger than 20 of 20, top third'. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: the gate moved from 14:30 to 14:45 and the question joined trend/leg_aging: at 15:00 the leg since 14:00 is TREND-05's 60-minute move.

title: One-way hour, signed
source: net60 = C[t]-C[t-60]; path = sum_{i=0..11}|C[t-5i]-C[t-5i-5]|; eff = net60/path. |net60| bottom third vs this minute = 'no hour move'; else direction = sign(net60), one-way if |eff| ranks top half against the prior sessions at this minute whose own |net60| is above their bottom third, else two-way. Field: close of state/spx_jev/bars (or store spx_bars).
notes: price.hour_one_way is close but measures crossings of the hourly average, not net/summed-5-min efficiency; use bars. History: store spx_bars has 66 sessions (07-06 on), live bars files only 12 days. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: the efficiency is ranked only against the hours that moved (an hour that went nowhere made 'one-way' near automatic, 45 to 14); moved from trend/trend_vs_chop to trend/leg_aging, since it carries TREND-09's 60-minute sign.

title: Have the day's 5-minute moves followed through or reversed each other, around the day's own drift?
source: price.day_character
notes: exact match: the variance-ratio sentence ends 'top third: building / middle: mixed / bottom: cancelling'. Omitted until 12 5-min returns since 10:00 (~11:00). Question pressure test 2026-10-07: retitled and the answers renamed (building = followed-through, cancelling = reversed): the drift-adjusted variance ratio measures follow-through against reversal, not a trend day (10-05, a steady up day, read 'cancelling'). The measure is unchanged.

title: Move speeding up or fading
source: d20 = C[t-10]-C[t-30]; d10 = C[t]-C[t-10]; ratio = sign(d20)*d10 / (|d20|/2); tol = 0.05 x the read's sigma. |d20| <= tol: None (no leg to age). 'reversing' when ratio < 0 and |d10| > tol; else ratio ranked against the prior sessions' non-negative ratios at this minute: top third accelerating, middle steady, bottom fading. Every answer leads with d20's side.
notes: momentum.pace is unsigned and compares 10 vs the previous 10 minutes (not 20) with fixed 2/3 and 1.5 cuts, so it cannot give 'reversing'. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: the tolerance rose from 0.02 to 0.05 sigma ('reversing' fired on 38 of 99 reads after any wiggle following a ~1.4-point leg), the answer carries d20's side, and the rank is against prior non-negative ratios only. Its own group trend/pace_change (decided in step 1, not in the decisions): leg_aging would hold four members sharing one vote, three of them the 60-minute leg, which would dilute this 10-against-20-minute reversal to a quarter vote.

title: Pullback in the leg, signed
source: 60-min window [t-60,t]: net = C[t]-C[t-60]; leg only if |net| > this minute's median |net| on prior sessions. Up leg: ext = max high in window at minute i; push = ext-C[t-60]; giveback = (ext-C[t])/push; deep = giveback > this minute's median giveback; fast = the extreme is 5+ minutes old, (ext-C[t])/(60-i) > push/i, and giveback >= half this minute's median giveback. Mirror for down legs.
notes: two medians (leg size, giveback) per minute-of-day from prior sessions; spx_bars store covers it. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: an extreme 2-3 minutes old divided by 2-3 made a 2-5% give-back read 'fast' (18 of 43 deep-or-fast): 'fast' now needs 5 minutes since the extreme and half the usual give-back. It anchors trend/leg_aging.

title: 60-minute range sweep: held or failed
source: H/L = max high / min low over bars [t-70,t-10); break up if max high of bars [t-10,t) > H + 0.02*sigma (fixed tolerance); held if C[t] > H else failed; mirror for down. sigma = read's sigma.
notes: no history needed; tolerance value (0.02 sigma here) is a design choice to fix.

title: Biggest 1-minute bar vs normal
source: ratio = max(high-low) / median(high-low) over the last 30 finished 1-min bars; rank vs same minute prior sessions (cut points e.g. <2/3 normal, 2/3-90% large, >=90% burst).
notes: price.minute_width only compares the current minute to today's typical minute with a fixed 2x cut; shock.burst is 5-minute moves. Use bars. Bars volume field is 0 for SPX (index), so no volume weighting.

title: Latest leg with or against the day
source: price.prior_close_push
notes: second tercile (distance from yesterday's close) bottom 'near it' = flat day; else 'away from' = with, 'toward' = against. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: the 'quiet leg' answer (the first tercile's bottom) is gone: it was TREND-01's bottom tercile counted again.

title: Straddle held up vs clock decay
source: vol.straddle_vs_clock
notes: tercile of 'times its usual share ... higher than k of n sessions at this minute'. Missing on 10-06 (row carried no straddle). Question pressure test 2026-10-07: dark on 10-06 and 10-07: the read row carried no straddle (range_ruler.em_points). The parser is right; the fix is upstream (operations, step 3).

title: Last 30 min swing vs same half hour
source: vol.realized_vs_clock
notes: current template uses fifths (bottom fifth quiet / between ordinary / top fifth busy); 09-28 reads used terciles. vol.realized_vs_clock_rank is the same idea as a pace ratio.

Question pressure test 2026-10-07: dark on 10-06 and 10-07 for lack of the lob_flow tape (operations, step 3); the mapping is right.

title: Put tilt vs same minute
source: skew.put_tilt_vs_usual
notes: words 'a steep put tilt / a usual tilt / a flat tilt'; 'calls are priced above puts, a call tilt' = tilted to calls. An older template ('steeper than k of n, past the flat rank') ran on early days and is mapped from its rank at the label's fifths (cuts.SKEW_STEEP_RANK 0.8, SKEW_FLAT_RANK 0.2; it cut at thirds before 2026-10-07). Dark on 10-06/07 (no lob_flow tape).

source: vol.vvix_vs_vix
notes: label ranks the size of the leftover only; sign = (VVIX change - explained), parsed from the two numbers. Leftover under the median = about as much; at/above median = more or less by sign.

title: Priced move loaded by an event
source: vol.ruler_event_load
notes: ruler part: 'this morning's sigma ruler is X times its N-session median ... (bottom|middle|top) third' = compressed/normal/swollen (vs prior mornings, once a day). Event part: only the calendar rows named with the ruler-loading events' words (labels/vol.py LOADING_EVENTS: the Fed's rate decision, the chair's testimony, Jackson Hole), at HH:MM against the read time; '; none of them is' in the label (its own clause, from about 10-02) = no event. Answer = '<ruler>, <event>'. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: every calendar row counted as an event (the 09-30 quarter-end close made every read 'event ahead'). The straddle outage (dark 10-06/07) is upstream (step 3).

source: price.day_move_split
notes: side + tercile ('near it / away from it / far from it'). Question pressure test 2026-10-07: position only: the gap-or-trading part read 'mostly trading' by default (17 of 28 'near the close' reads wrong) and repeated LEVELS-01 in the same group.

source: levels.prior_day

Question pressure test 2026-10-07: 'no bar has gone more than' the break buffer = inside (it read 'break holding' with no real break); price back inside after breaking both edges = the failed break of the side broken more recently: the first-hour label gives each break's minutes ago, the box label ('broke out both ways and came back') does not, so the bars say which side a close last broke past (the label's own rule: the box edge plus measures.move_bar).

notes: only on premarket-lane reads; live/tape reads must carry the day's last premarket value (09:28 checkpoint). Live reads take the day's last premarket read. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: one missing premarket read emptied the whole day (59-60 of 70); the night's own /ES bars now stand in.

source: From 10:05: R30 = max high - min low of the 09:35-10:04 bars in points, ranked against the same window on the prior sessions in terciles (narrow/normal/wide); None before 10:05.
notes: fixed window, so ranking is vs prior sessions' same window. Ranked in points (prior sessions' sigma is not in the bars). Question pressure test 2026-10-07: the first-five-minute answers are gone: the 'pace' was never computed, the source said sigma while the code ranked points, and 'busy' never fired.

source: levels.break_armed

source: gex.flip_distance
notes: side from 'sigma above/below the gamma flip'; bottom third = near, middle = above/below, top = far. Units are sigma, not expected-move units (ranking is unit-free). Question pressure test 2026-10-07: answered only while the read's diary row is SPX's own book (gex_source 'native'): on 10-06 and 10-07 every row was a SPY stand-in scaled by a factor that changed each minute, ranked against real SPX sessions.

notes: Question pressure test 2026-10-07: answered only while the read's diary row is SPX's own book (gex_source 'native'): on 10-06 and 10-07 every row was a SPY stand-in scaled by a factor that changed each minute, ranked against real SPX sessions. Until step 2 (2026-10-08) it parsed the grip clause of gex.magnet_distance (the heaviest strike's top-strike share, the whole 0DTE book, a day flag: 89% of reads carried the day's usual answer) and cast no vote; since step 2 the builder measures the share of gamma near spot itself from the stored diary rows, live and in backfill alike, the label sentence unchanged, and it votes. The 0-7DTE books are not in the diary's per-strike gamma, so the 0DTE book stands for them.

source: gex.magnet_distance
notes: strike 'above price' means SPX is below it. bottom third 'seated on it' = on it. PARTIAL: the after-14:00 1DTE magnet is dark (expiry_calendar: 'the SPX scan writes no 1DTE slice'). source: The lob-flow collector's refill test (lob_flow/agg/{day}.jsonl, the readings by the read, the newest within 3 minutes): of the book's magnet and walls hit 3 times or more in its last 15 minutes, the nearest to spot, when within one 30-minute expected move of it (the read's sigma x sqrt(30/390)); its refill share (refilled / hits) ranked against the same minute's nearest contested strike (3 hits or more) on the trailing sessions (at least 10): at or above the middle = defended, below = abandoned; above / below by the strike's side of spot.
notes: Missing 10-06 (no lob_flow tape). Question pressure test 2026-10-07: its own group options/strike_defense (directional; it shared the shared/pinned vote). Until step 2 (2026-10-08) it parsed options.strike_defense, whose reach is a top-third rank against other sessions' nearest strikes (often right at price, so a strike 5-12 points away was out of reach) and whose minimum is 10 hits; since step 2 the builder reads the collector's record itself with a fixed reach and a 3-hit minimum, live and in backfill alike, the label sentence unchanged. DRAFT: the 3-hit minimum and the reach are the decision's, not measured cuts.

source: options.flow_lean_30

source: gex.charm_wall_distance

source: The diary row's heaviest call-side and put-side gamma strikes of today's 0DTE book (gex_views.call_wall_gamma / put_wall_gamma, reversion/{day}.jsonl) at the read against the newest row written by 30 minutes before it (within 5 minutes): a shift under one strike step (5 points) stayed put; both stayed put = stand still; both moved the same way = both moved up / down; else the pair's width grew = spread out, shrank = pulled in.
notes: Question pressure test 2026-10-07: answered only while the read's diary row is SPX's own book (gex_source 'native'): on 10-06 and 10-07 every row was a SPY stand-in scaled by a factor that changed each minute, ranked against real SPX sessions. title: Opening type
source: 09:30-09:59 1-min bars; the settled open = the 09:31 bar's open; references: prior session high/low (store spx_bars) and overnight /ES high/low converted to SPX by the 09:30 /ES-SPX basis (state/spx_jev/overnight). Drive up (down) = the settled open in the bottom (top) 10% of the 30-min range, the close in the opposite 20%, and no later bar's low (high) back through the open by more than 0.05 sigma; test-then-drive = a bar tags a reference level (within 0.05 sigma) before the first close reaches the far 20%, and the half hour closes there; else rotation. Answers from 10:30.
notes: rules are not written anywhere yet; thresholds above are a DRAFT. Answer is fixed for the rest of the day. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: 'drive' had no side, the open-edge test was near automatic (6 of 8 days, on the 09:30 bar's stale open) and test-then-drive never fired; from 10:30 (at 10:00 its window is TREND-02's). Judge it in sessions (30+), not reads.

source: premarket.legs (premarket lane)

('N moved, all with the night's rise: one way' / 'split; the latest with...' / 'the latest against...' / 'Only one finished leg' / 'No finished leg' or 'net move is quiet' = night quiet). notes: direction words 'ahead in the stocks-up / stocks-down direction / in line'; contrarian read applied downstream. Roll withholding: label is omitted across a /MBT roll. The contrarian lean is for the reader, not the answer.

title: Trend vs chop, last 30 min
source: SPX 1-min closes: |net move| / sum of |1-min moves| over the last 30 minutes, or since 09:35 before 10:05; ranked against the same measure at the same minute on the trailing 20 sessions (at least 10): top third clean, middle mixed, bottom choppy.
notes: Fix applied: before 10:05 the window runs from the settled open (09:35), so it replaces opening_chop on the tape lane. Needs 25 bars (5 before 10:05).

title: VWAP balance: one-sided or orbiting
source: SPY minute bars (state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl for prior sessions; the day's own quotes live, its volume the siege box's minute volume), closes only: session VWAP = cumulative close x volume / volume; at each 5-minute mark (09:35, 09:40, ...) SPY's close above or below its VWAP; minutes since the last mark on the other side, and the side flips between the marks of the last 30 minutes; each ranked against the same measure at the same minute on the trailing 20 sessions (at least 10). Flips top third = orbiting; else minutes-since top third = long above / long below VWAP (the latest mark's side); else recently crossed.
notes: VWAP is volume-weighted from SPY's own minute volume (SPX bars carry none), on closes so the live quotes and the saved bars agree. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: 'long one-sided' now names its side; the touch count (closes within 0.01% of VWAP, which depended on how often prices arrive: live and saved bars disagreed on 10-07 10:01) is replaced by the side flips at the 5-minute marks; joined flow/vwap_stretch with FLOW-01, whose VWAP side it repeats once it has one. DRAFT: the orbiting-first precedence.

title: Volume spike follow-through, signed
source: SPY volume per finished 5-minute slot (09:30-09:34, ...) of the last 30 minutes; a slot whose volume is at or above the 90th percentile of the same slot on the trailing 20 sessions (at least 10) is a spike; the latest spike's SPX direction = close - open over the slot (0 = none), held when the latest SPX close is past the slot's high-low midpoint in that direction, else faded, both signed. The read's day's SPY volume is the siege box's minute volume (state/siege/baseline.json), the same figures as the saved minute bars.
notes: Fix applied: volume from SPY's minute bars ({CTX}), since $SPX has none. DRAFT: the 90th-percentile cut (the question's 'top 10%'). Question pressure test 2026-10-07: live volume came from ~70-second quote snapshots (about 22% above the saved bars, in lumps: 4 of 12 live spikes on 10-07 were not in the bars); the siege box's minute volumes match the bars exactly. 'Spike faded' is split by side; a flat spike slot is 'none'.

title: Range compressing or expanding
source: SPX 1-min bars: high-low range of the last 30 minutes over the range of the 30 minutes before it; ranked against the same measure at the same minute on the trailing 20 sessions (at least 10): bottom third compressed, top expanded.
notes: Needs 25 bars in each half hour, so None before 10:30.

title: Compressed range: coiled or resting
source: Only when VOLATILITY-04 reads compressed (else None). Coiled when any of: a ruler-loading event (labels/vol.py LOADING_EVENTS) due within 60 minutes on the calendar; iv.trend_30min on the read says at-the-money implied volatility rose or fell past its flat band; the ten-year yield's move since the prior close ($TNX against its prior daily close) ranks in the top third against the same minute on the trailing 20 sessions (at least 10; judgment.YieldMove.fired's rule); BREADTH-09 reads 'in play'. Resting when none fires; None when none could be measured.
notes: New in the question pressure test 2026-10-07: the code version of the dropped JEV question quiet_coiled_or_resting (VOLATILITY-15, whose criteria were this fixed OR of code facts, applied loosely). It shares VOLATILITY-04's group, so a compressed range still casts one vote. The cheap checks run first; BREADTH-09 is measured only when they are all quiet. DRAFT: the 60-minute event window.

title: VIX open vs what the gap implies
source: $VIX and SPX minute bars (state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl (prior sessions; the day's own bars cut at the read, or context/{day}.jsonl quotes live)): the 09:35 VIX (the 09:34 bar's close) less (the prior session's last VIX + VIX_PER_GAP_PCT x the gap from the prior close to the settled open in percent); ranked against the same measure on the trailing 20 sessions (at least 10): top third richer, bottom cheaper.
notes: Fix applied: the 09:35 VIX print, not the first diary print; walk-forward (prior sessions only). Opening reads only: reads from 09:35 to 10:35 answer, later ones None. DRAFT: VIX_PER_GAP_PCT = -1.7 points per 1% gap (labels/vol.py's -1.7 per sigma, a sigma near 1%).

title: Gap size in implied units
source: SPX bars (bars/ and store spx_bars, 60 sessions): gap = settled open (09:34 close) - prior close; implied one-day move = prior close x prior-close $VIX (daily_closes) / 100 / sqrt(252); |gap / implied| ranked against the same on the trailing 60 sessions (at least 10): bottom third small, middle normal, top large, signed by the gap. Answers the opening reads only (09:35-10:35).
notes: Fix applied: the prior-close VIX / sqrt(252) ruler and a 60-session rank. The premarket half (/ES vs 16:00 before 09:35) is not built: the live lane has no read before 09:35. LEVELS-01 keeps its own gap-fill answer. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: answers only the opening reads (it repeated one day answer on every read); moved into levels/prior_close with LEVELS-01/02, since it measures the same gap size and side (V 0.88).

title: Front VIX curve shape
source: $VIX9D / $VIX at the read (state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl (prior sessions; the day's own bars cut at the read, or context/{day}.jsonl quotes live)): at or above 1.00 = inverted; else ranked against the same measure at the same minute on the trailing 20 sessions (at least 10): bottom third calm, otherwise normal.
notes: Fix applied: ranked against the sessions on file (the context bars, from 2026-08-11), not a year; VIX/VIX3M is not used as a fallback. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: no vote ("votes": false): inversion is a rare stress state nothing else measures, kept on record; as a level that holds all day it took half of front_curve's vote and weighed in the matcher as a day fingerprint.

title: Vol fails to confirm a new extreme
source: SPX bars: a session high (low) set in the last 30 minutes beyond the extreme of the bars before them (new_extreme_vs_prior_swing: at least 30 earlier bars, the earlier swing's own extreme, not the runner-up a minute before); $VIX (state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl for prior sessions; the day's own bars cut at the read, or context/{day}.jsonl quotes live) at the new extreme's minute against VIX at the earlier extreme's: a new high with VIX lower, or a new low with VIX higher, or VIX within 0.05 points either way, confirms; else VIX diverges. Mechanical first: the read in the last hour (from 15:00), the monthly expiry (the third Friday) or a pre-holiday session, or a calendar row in its first 15 minutes. No new extreme: None (LEVELS-05 says it).
notes: Converted from JEV to code. Same-day ATM IV is not read (VIX only). Shares one vote with BREADTH-03. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: it compared VIX with the runner-up bar 1-3 minutes earlier, so ties flipped between live and backfill; 'no new extreme' repeated LEVELS-05 in a second group and is now None; the answer names its side; every Friday was mechanical, now only the third.

title: Recent days' range regime
source: daily_closes/$SPX.jsonl (sessions before the day): daily range = (high - low) / close; the mean of the last 5 sessions ranked against the trailing 60 sessions' rolling 5-session means: bottom third quiet, top wide.
notes: Ranked against recent sessions (60), per Will's note. The context fields (10-session trend strength, intraday character) are not stored: the matrix holds answers only. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: no vote ("votes": false): about one answer change a week with no 30-60 minute mechanism; regime context, not a voter.

title: Overnight range position
source: The read's /ES quote (market_context) against the night's /ES high and low (overnight/{day}.jsonl, session != regular, 1-minute bars only, bars before 09:30). Roll guard: the quote more than 2% from the night's last bar is another contract, so None.
notes: 147 nights on disk; the guard's 2% is a DRAFT. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: the night files hold 5-minute bars beside the 1-minute ones; the loader keeps bar_minutes == 1 only (found in the MACRO-08 review).

title: Room to the next barrier
source: In the direction of SPX's last 30-minute move, the distance (share of price) to the nearest level beyond price by more than 0.02 sigma: the prior session's high, low and close, the night's /ES high and low moved onto SPX by the 09:30 basis, the session's high and low before the last 30 minutes, the next round number (25-point steps); ranked against the same measure at the same minute on the trailing 20 sessions (at least 10): bottom third close, top far.
notes: Walls and VWAP are not in the level library yet (no wall history for the prior sessions; the S11 library is not built), so the rank is over the same levels on every session. DRAFT: the 25-point round numbers. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: the last 30 minutes' own new high counted as the nearest barrier, so 'close' repeated LEVELS-05: today's high and low are taken from before the half hour, and a level within 0.02 sigma of price is passed over. DRAFT: the 0.02 sigma.

title: Which side is tiring at a tested edge or extreme
source: Edges: today's high and low before the last 30 minutes, the prior session's high and low. A test = a run of bars reaching within 0.05 sigma of the edge; an edge with 2+ runs in the last 30 minutes (the latest-tested wins). First run vs latest: depth past the edge, mean SPY volume per bar of the run, rejection (the extreme against the closes of the 3 bars after); the latest shallower, lighter and sharper-rejected on 2 of 3 = buyers tiring at a high edge, sellers tiring at a low edge; when either run has no bar after it yet, shallower and lighter both.
notes: Converted from JEV to code without the S11 test ledger: the three ratios compare the latest test with the first directly, not ranked against the time of day. The weaker-extreme field (J2-02) is not stored. DRAFT thresholds: 0.05 sigma touch, 3 rejection bars, 2 of 3. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: summed volume made longer tests look heavier (now the mean per bar), and a run ending on the last bar scored rejection 0, which leaned the answer to 'neither'; layer 2, a discrete label.

title: Wall test in the last hour
source: The day's SPX diary rows (reversion/{day}.jsonl) at each bar of the last 60 minutes: the near gamma walls (gex_views.call_wall_gamma / put_wall_gamma); a bar whose high-low reaches within 0.10 sigma (the label's touch rule) of a wall touches it; the latest touch's wall, with price now at or on the held side (at or below a call wall, at or above a put wall) = held, else broke.
notes: Shares the held-or-failed vote. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: it read the far open-interest walls (100+ points away) and answered 'no touch' on 94 of 94 reads; it reads the near gamma walls the diary already stores. Answered only while the read's diary row is spx's own book (gex_source 'native'): on 10-06 and 10-07 every row was a spy stand-in scaled by a factor that changed each minute, ranked against real spx sessions.

title: Pin holding or breaking loose
source: The diary's magnet, 0DTE and 1-to-7-day walls and near gamma walls at the read; over the last 60 minutes' SPX closes, a level crossed 3+ times is the pin (the most crossed); price now more than one 30-minute expected move (sigma x sqrt(30/390)) from it = broke loose; the distance now wider than the median earlier swing (swings of 2+ bars, the hour's first left out) and the current swing longer, with the distance past a quarter of the expected move = stretching; else holding.
notes: Moved from JEV to code. DRAFT: 3 crossings, medians of the earlier swings. Shares the pinned vote. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: 'stretching' fired 31 to 4 against 'holding' because a swing that had come back still counted as wide: the distance is today's, earlier one-bar swings and the window's cut first swing are left out, and stretching needs a quarter of the expected move. Answered only while the read's diary row is spx's own book (gex_source 'native'): on 10-06 and 10-07 every row was a spy stand-in scaled by a factor that changed each minute, ranked against real spx sessions. DRAFT: the quarter.

title: Same-day option quote width
source: The lob-flow collector's quote sweeps (state/lob_flow/raw/{day}/sweeps.jsonl(.gz)): the nearest-the-money bucket's quoted spread (25-40 delta, after ~13:10 the 10-25 one), rounded to the cent; the median of the last 5 minutes' sweeps in the newest sweep's bucket, ranked against the prior sessions quoting the same bucket at the same minute (at least 10), ties counted half: under a third tight, under two thirds normal, under 0.9 wide, else very wide.
notes: The sweep carries no vega, so the spread is ranked in dollars, not per unit of vega. 21 days of sweeps on file. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: the ranks rested on floating-point leftovers around 5-cent ticks. Of the two fixes offered, the rank within the same bucket with half-counted ties was chosen (step 1): fixed tick cuts would read every afternoon as tight, since the stand-in 10-25 bucket quotes about half the 25-40 bucket's width (0.05 against 0.10 on file).

title: NYSE breadth beyond the day move (live lane)
source: The read's derived advance-decline ($ADVN - $DECN only: the one same-day breadth figure Schwab serves right) against SPX's move since the prior close: on the trailing 20 sessions at this minute the line (the derived one, else the saved $ADD, clean next day, from state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl (prior sessions; the day's own bars cut at the read, or context/{day}.jsonl quotes live)) is regressed on the move; today's residual ranked against the sessions' residuals: top third stronger, bottom weaker.
notes: Live lane only (the derived line is the live reading). Needs 10 sessions with both; the store's $ADVN starts 09-28, the context bars files earlier.

title: Breadth and small caps confirm a new extreme
source: A new session high (low) in the last 30 minutes beyond the extreme before them (new_extreme_vs_prior_swing, as VOLATILITY-14); three confirmations: the derived advance-decline now above (below) its level at the earlier extreme's minute; IWM's close within 0.05% of its own session high (low) of closes; the 8 largest names' weighted return from the earlier extreme's minute to now positive (negative); 2 of 3 = confirmed. No new extreme: None (LEVELS-05 says it). Weights: state/spx_leaders/weights.json, the entry dated on or before the day; prices from state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl (prior sessions; the day's own bars cut at the read, or context/{day}.jsonl quotes live).
notes: $VOLD leg replaced by the derived $ADVN - $DECN (nothing from the same-day-wrong list, nor $ADD). IWM's extreme is of closes, so live quotes and saved bars agree. Reads from the weights file's oldest entry (2026-08-21, the 10-06 shares backdated to when TSLA and BRK/B entered the feed) on; the old 'None before 2026-10-06' no longer holds. DRAFT: the 0.05% IWM tolerance. Shares one vote with VOLATILITY-14. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: the earlier extreme was the previous minute and the answer had no side.

title: Biggest heavyweight shock beyond SPX
source: The 8 largest names (weights dated on or before the day; GOOG summed into GOOGL, BRK/B as the feed names it): each one's 30-minute return less its usual multiple of SPX's (the slope of its 30-minute returns on SPX's over the prior sessions' half hours, at least 20 pairs); the largest weight x residual; |pull| ranked against the largest pull at the same minute on the trailing sessions: top third large, signed, else small.
notes: Weights are taken as of on or before the read's day (the task's rule), not strictly before as the question's note asked; the weights file (state/spx_leaders/weights.json) holds the 2026-10-06 entry and a 2026-08-21 one (the same approximate shares, backdated to the day TSLA and BRK/B entered the feed, so the heavyweight questions have history); reads before 08-21 are None. TSLA and BRK/B are in the feed since 08-21. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: the 'followed / alone' split is gone: each of its four large answers held 3-6 reads, and 'followed' counted any follower however small.

title: Heavyweight in play since the close (gate)
source: Each of the 8 largest names' return since the prior session's close less its usual multiple (BREADTH-07's) of SPX's since the same close, weighted; |largest pull| top third at this minute against the trailing sessions = in play, up or down by the pull's sign; the rest of the index (SPX's move less the names' weighted moves) followed when it has the pull's sign and is above the bottom third of its own.
options: in play up, rest did not
in play down, rest did not
notes: Gate for the heavyweight_catalyst_or_flow judgment question (BREADTH-10) and a VOLATILITY-18 input; "votes": false: computed and stored, no vote (until 2026-10-07 the '(gate, no vote)' group name was text only and it voted, a near-constant answer, 68 of 70). Since step 2 (2026-10-08) the answer carries the pull's side ('in play up' / 'in play down'), which the heavyweight question's stored pick is signed by (answer_matrix.row_answers). The rank's history uses the same since-close residual (since_close_beyond) with today's fitted links as today's value (checked in step 1). DRAFT: the 30-minute multiple stands in for a since-the-close one.

title: Volume backs the move
source: Over the last 30 minutes the share of SPY's minute volume (state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl for prior sessions; the read's day's from the siege box's minute volumes, state/siege/baseline.json) traded in the minutes SPX's bar closed the way the half hour went (close - open of the window); ranked against the same measure at the same minute on the trailing 20 sessions (at least 10): top third confirmed, bottom diverging, both signed by the half hour's move; middle balanced.
notes: A flat half hour (net 0) is None. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: signed; live volume came from ~70-second quote snapshots while training used minute bars, now the siege box's minute volumes for both; joined trend/last_30m_move with TREND-01 and FLOW-07, since once signed it carries TREND-01's 30-minute sign (its own information is the volume share; judge it on that).

title: Price travel per volume
source: SPX points travelled (sum of |1-min moves|) over the last 30 minutes per million SPY shares (state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl for prior sessions; the read's day's from the siege box's minute volumes); None when fewer than 24 of the 30 minutes carry SPY volume; ranked against the same measure at the same minute on the trailing 20 sessions (at least 10): bottom third heavy with little travel, top easy travel on light volume.
notes: Amihud thinness. Keep only if < 0.8 with FLOW-05 and VOLATILITY-02 (not measured here). Question pressure test 2026-10-07: it divided by quote-snapshot volume (up to double the bars', or near zero after an outage); the siege box's minute volumes now, and a 24-minute coverage floor.

title: Volume pace vs clock
source: volume.spy_pace_30
notes: k / n from 'higher than k of the last n sessions at this minute': bottom third light, top heavy. The label is SPY's volume over the half hour against the same half hour on the prior sessions on file.

title: Volume profile location
source: The last 5 sessions' profile: SPY's minute volume (state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl) summed into 5-point bins of SPX's close; a bin at or above the 75th percentile of bin volume is a high-volume node. SPX's last close above or below every bin = outside the profile; in a node = at a node; else the nearer node above or below (equally near = at a node).
notes: 5 sessions kept. DRAFT: 5-point bins, the quartile cuts. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: new ground was filed as 'low-volume node' (36 of 94), ties leaned 'below', and five answers were too thin for ~60 reads. DRAFT marks kept.

title: Index move alignment
source: SPY, QQQ and IWM 30-minute returns: prior sessions from state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl; the read's day from its quote snapshots (context/{day}.jsonl), live and in backfill alike; each |return| ranked against its own at this minute: a move above the bottom third counts, signed; all three moved the same way = same way up / down; movers both ways = in conflict; no mover = none moved; else mixed.
notes: Rebuilt on QQQ and IWM (no /NQ, /RTY). Question pressure test 2026-10-07: signed; live and graded agreed on only 84 of 99 reads, so the read's day is built from its quotes in backfill too; joined trend/last_30m_move (its sign is TREND-01's; its own information is the three indexes agreeing).

title: Outside markets ahead of SPX, 30 min
source: /ZN, HYG, USO and GLD (state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl (prior sessions; the day's own bars cut at the read, or context/{day}.jsonl quotes live)): each one's 30-minute return beyond its usual multiple of SPX's (BREADTH-07's fit), divided by its residual spread and signed by the multiple's sign (its usual link with stocks), averaged; ranked against the same measure at the same minute on the trailing 20 sessions (at least 10): top fifth up, bottom fifth down, else no clear lean.
notes: Fix applied: /6E dropped, /ZN added; a session without /ZN bars (a bond holiday) is None. The label's hour-by-hour minute link is replaced by the usual multiple's sign.

title: SPX vs what bonds imply since the close
source: SPX's return since the prior close less beta x /ZN's since its 16:00 close (state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl (prior sessions; the day's own bars cut at the read, or context/{day}.jsonl quotes live); beta = the slope of SPX's close-to-close returns on /ZN's over the trailing sessions, at least 10); |gap| ranked against the same at this minute: bottom third nowhere; SPX short of what bonds imply = up, past it = down; the top fifth (rank 0.8+) = far up / far down.
notes: Runs on /ZN. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: no vote ("votes": false): as a voter it was the day's since-close move relabelled (V 0.72-0.86 with LEVELS) and diluted MACRO-01, which now holds macro/macro_gap alone. Kept computed for the macro_gap judgment gate; the rank share it gates on is exposed in the answer itself (step 1's choice of 'expose the rank share'): 'far up / far down' is the top fifth, so judgment.py can gate on rank >= 0.8 from the answers it already reads. Since step 2 (2026-10-08) the macro_gap gate fires only on 'far up' / 'far down', once until the answer changes, and its label states the gap's size and side (code_features_market.macro_gap).

title: Rates tape busy vs normal
source: /ZN's volume over the last 30 minutes (state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl (prior sessions; the day's own bars cut at the read, or context/{day}.jsonl quotes live)) ranked against the same half hour on the trailing sessions: bottom third quiet, top busy.
notes: The 10-minute companion is not built. Fold into VOLATILITY-02 if > 0.8.

title: Event-day phase
source: Fixed tier map on calendar/events.json: high = FOMC, FOMC_PRESSER, CPI, JOBS, PCE; medium = PPI, RETAIL_SALES, GDP, ISM_MANUFACTURING, ISM_SERVICES, JOLTS, FOMC_MINUTES, FED_CHAIR_TESTIMONY, FED_CHAIR_JACKSON_HOLE, CONSUMER_CONFIDENCE, UMICH_SENTIMENT. In order: a high-tier row today; the next trading day high (eve); the previous trading day high (day after); a medium row today; else ordinary. Uncovered days are None.
notes: Fix applied: a fixed tier map instead of a learned yearly ranking. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: when only one neighbouring day was outside the calendar the read leaked through as medium or ordinary: an uncovered next day is None before the eve check, an uncovered previous day before the day-after check.

title: Follow-through after the latest release
source: The latest calendar row (Fed speakers' remarks left out) whose first 15 minutes are over, within 120 minutes of the read (Fed statement and presser are separate rows). In the session: SPX closes at the row's start (the first bar's open for a 09:30 row), 15 minutes after, and now; before the open: /ES night bars at those minutes and the read's /ES quote as now (else the night's last /ES bar). Back through the start = reversed, named by the way price went; past the 15-minute price by more than 0.05 of the normal-day sigma (rulers.normal_day_sigma, as the premarket lane stamps it) = extended; else held/faded; each signed by the first reaction.
notes: Release types pooled (data, the Fed statement and the presser). The rank against past releases is not applied: the verdict uses the fixed 0.05-sigma rule of labels/events_shocks.py. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: it had no side, so the direction stage averaged it to zero; Fed speeches counted as releases; its sigma was the read's own, not the label rule's normal-day sigma. A first reaction of exactly 0 has no side: None.

title: Month-turn rebalance side and size
source: The day's place among the month's trading days (sessions.is_trading_day): the first 3 = new-month inflow; the last 2 = the month-to-date $SPX minus TLT return (daily_closes, the last close before the day against the prior month's last close) ranked against every full month on file: top fifth sell big, then sell, small, buy, bottom fifth buy big; other days None.
notes: Fix applied: the daily-closes job's $SPX and TLT closes (from 2016) replace the hard-coded flows.rebalance_side. Shadow. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: on the month's last 2 days the gap is measured once, through the last close before the first of them (ranks of 0.78 and 0.805 straddled the 0.8 cut, so one month's size changed between its two days).

title: Leveraged ETF bull/bear tilt
source: SPXL and TQQQ (bull) against SPXS and SQQQ (bear): each fund's 30-minute share volume over its own median at this minute on the prior sessions (state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl), bull and bear the equal-weight means, tilt = (bull - bear) / (bull + bear), less what SPX's 30-minute move predicts (a line fitted on the prior sessions' half hours, at least 20); the residual ranked against the same measure at the same minute on the trailing 20 sessions (at least 10): top third high, bottom low. None on a live read (the day's bars not saved yet).
notes: The four funds are in the feed since 08-21 (thin, missing a few minutes a day). Read contrarian by the learners, not here. Question pressure test 2026-10-07: quote volume ran ~21% high on SPXL live (3 of 13 reads flipped) and the dollar share leaned high (50 to 8) from the bear funds' decay and TQQQ/SQQQ's size: each fund now against its own usual. It answers only once the day's bars are saved, so no live read has an answer: no vote ("votes": false, step 1's decision, as the critic counted it). Drop it if it is still at or below the null after ~20 more days.
